title: Assurance must be derived from evidence, not asserted
description:
PROBLEM

Claim is a plain struct with public fields, so any attestor can type an assurance level as a literal. fido2.rs:83-90 writes 'assurance: Iaa3, presence: PresenceLevel::Hardware' for a device that is merely reachable over HID. oidc.rs:82-88 writes Iaa2 from a JWT payload whose signature was never checked. Nothing in the type system distinguishes an assurance level that was proven from one that was typed.

The review (persona-5s4b) found this pattern three times independently. It will recur, because the codebase makes asserting free and proving optional.

ROOT CAUSE

enumerate() returns Vec<Claim>. A Claim carries assurance and presence - the two things prove() is supposed to establish. So the cheap discovery call produces the same type as the expensive proof call, and the daemon cannot tell them apart. prove() being unimplemented is a tracked deferral; enumerate() answering the question prove() was meant to answer is the defect.

CONSTRAINT

An assurance level and a presence level may exist only as the output of verifying evidence. Make the alternative uncompilable rather than reviewable.

Sketch (exact shape open):
- enumerate() stops returning Claim. It returns a weaker Candidate: source, spiffe_id, display_name - no assurance, no presence.
- Claim gains private fields and no public literal construction.
- The only way to obtain a Claim is prove(), which takes a Candidate plus evidence and returns Claim.
- Assurance and presence are derived from the evidence variant, not passed in: hardware presence requires a witness carrying the touch timestamp, Iaa2 requires a token whose signature was verified, Iaa3 requires both.
- An attestor with no prove() implementation yields Candidates and therefore cannot contribute an assurance level at all. The daemon declines instead of asserting - which is the correct behaviour today and is currently not what happens.

WHY A CONSTRAINT AND NOT A FIX

Patching .30 and .49 individually leaves the shape that produced them. Any future attestor - PIV, GOA, Windows Hello - can make the same mistake, and the next review has to catch it again by reading. Removing the ability to assert deletes the category.

SUBSUMES (verified, not assumed)
  .49 fido2 Iaa3 + Hardware from HID enumeration - becomes uncompilable
  .30 oidc Iaa2 from unverified JWT - Iaa2 would require a verified-token witness
  .55 attacker-chosen authority: the trust domain is likewise derived from unverified iss;
      same rule extended to identity fields, not just assurance

DOES NOT SUBSUME - these are separate defects, do not close them against this
  .41 consumer attestation and pseudonymity unwired (issuance-path wiring)
  .47 presence gate read from audience[0] (request handling)
  .71 unrecognised presence requirement fails open (parsing)
  .105 prove() hands out a live IdP bearer token (credential handling)

ACCEPTANCE
  - No public path constructs a Claim with an assurance or presence value not derived from evidence.
  - Removing every prove() implementation still compiles, and the daemon then issues nothing above the lowest tier - verified by a test.
  - fido2.rs and oidc.rs cannot be restored to their current form without a compile error.

Filed from review persona-5s4b. Spec cross-reference: SPEC-HIA.md ## Assurance Levels (:303).
